I'm a health-focused data scientist with hands-on healthcare systems experience and an 
MSc in Computer Science with AI, focused on turning messy clinical data into equitable models and evidence.
I write my analyses as reproducible pipelines in line with the NHS Reproducible
Analytical Pipelines (RAP) approach and publish the code.

Before moving into data science I spent eight years at the University of Oxford's simulation
training and research centre at the John Radcliffe Hospital (NHS FT), building the data
systems and technology behind clinical training. I have run an independent digital
consultancy since 2012.

My MSc thesis used accelerometry data from the Millennium Cohort Study to
examine how the duration and temporal structure of activity recordings affect
ADHD prediction, comparing interpretable and complex models and testing for
bias across subgroups. See [Projects](projects.qmd).

## Interests

Clinical prediction modelling · Model evaluation and calibration ·
Algorithmic fairness · Reproducible analytical pipelines · Neurodevelopmental
conditions
